For regions where constraints are frequently set, distortion is effectively controlled, with the patterns disturbed significantly. Comparing the 24 m to 39.6 m tank floor, which have similar constraints at the outer edge of the long belts, the maximum distortion increased with the increasing diameter, from 114.5 mm to 130.8 mm. More such belts are present in the 39.6 m case due to the larger size. For the 32 m diameter case, the maximum displacement in the normal direction is 158.5 mm, due to the lack of constraint on the outer edge. Therefore, it can be concluded that both diameter size and weld plate layout or constraint design play a significant role in distortion induced by the welding procedure. Figure 28. Tank preheating will condition the tank structure, foundation, pipes, pumps, and valves to a temperature above the molten salt freezing point, avoiding salt solidification and potential damage to tank pipes or components. This section presents a preheating analysis based on a typical tank preheating procedure and empirical temperature data from a molten salt hot tank during preheating.
